notes: Decode-only estimate. Prefill and time-to-first-token are not estimated in v1.
Formula: 200 GB/s * efficiency / (active weights 0.269 GB + batch 1 * KV 0.094 GB), then * batch for aggregate tokens/s.
Efficiency range 0.55-0.85 (likely 0.70) is a documented engineering assumption, not a measured constant.
The KV read uses the effective context and the memory estimate's KV range.
Batch assumes perfect continuous batching; small-batch real-world throughput may be lower.

assumptions.text: v1 is single-device: one GPU/chip or CPU. No multi-GPU, offload, or distributed serving.
OmniRun reads only metadata and safetensors/GGUF headers. No tensor payload is downloaded and pickle files are never read.
JSON memory values are bytes; bandwidth values are decimal GB/s (10^9 bytes/s).
Peak memory = stored weights + KV cache + runtime overhead. Prefill activation peaks are not modeled.
Runtime overhead is 0.25 GiB plus 5% / 10% / 20% of weights for min / likely / max; it covers runtime context, allocator, and decode workspace.
KV cache = 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * tokens * batch * dtype bytes; windowed layers cap tokens at their window. MLA uses its compressed latent formula.
Speed is decode-only: bandwidth * efficiency / (active weights + batch*KV). Prefill and TTFT are not estimated. Efficiency is a documented range, not measured.
FP16/INT8/4-bit alternatives are hypothetical weights-only sizes; they do not imply an artifact exists, is supported, or has a particular quality.
SUPPORTED is a documented architecture/runtime path with a version floor. It is not a real run and does not imply VERIFIED.
VERIFIED is empty in v1. No result can claim a recorded real run; GO never means verified.
Usable Apple Silicon memory is 75% of total RAM. The actual macOS wired limit varies with OS version, RAM size, and other apps.
